text: New plan for Maria: maintain goal, $70/week, 4 meals a day. Doctor first.
Reading guidelines.json for the rules that apply
Floors and caps are set: at least 1200 kcal, under 1500 mg sodium, 28 g fiber.

reasons.why: About 14 g of fiber per 1,000 kcal supports digestion, fullness and heart health.
Stricter added sugar limit (5% of calories) for diabetes.
reasons.source: American Diabetes Association, Standards of Care in Diabetes (Section 5: Facilitating Positive Health Behaviors) (https://diabetesjournals.org/care/issue/48/Supplement_1)

reasons.why: The DASH plan limits sodium to 1,500 mg a day to lower blood pressure.
Saturated fat under 6% of calories for people with high blood pressure.
Eating below this floor makes it hard to get enough nutrients and is not safe without medical supervision.
reasons.source: NIH NHLBI, Aim for a Healthy Weight: low calorie diets (https://www.nhlbi.nih.gov/health/educational/lose_wt/eat/calories.htm)

reasons.why: Foods you are allergic to are removed in code before any meal is planned.
Spreading carbs evenly, about 45 g per meal, keeps blood sugar steadier.
reasons.source: American Diabetes Association, Standards of Care in Diabetes (Section 5: Facilitating Positive Health Behaviors) (https://diabetesjournals.org/care/issue/48/Supplement_1)

reasons.why: A glycemic load of 20 or less per meal avoids sharp glucose spikes.
reasons.source: American Diabetes Association, Standards of Care in Diabetes (Section 5: Facilitating Positive Health Behaviors) (https://diabetesjournals.org/care/issue/48/Supplement_1)

reasons.why: At least 3,500 mg of potassium a day from food helps balance sodium.

constraints.summary: Maria's plan rules: At least 1200 kcal and 28 g fiber a day, under 1500 mg sodium, under 25 g added sugar, saturated fat under 6% of calories, at most 45 g carbs per meal, glycemic load 20 or less per meal, at least 3500 mg potassium.

text: Diabetes rules on: max 45 g carbs and glycemic load 20 per meal. Non negotiable.
